author: syou6162
body:
## 概要

コードベースのセルフレビューを実施し、品質向上とCI/CDパイプラインの改善を行いました。大規模な変更を`git-sequential-stage`ツールを使用してセマンティックな単位に分割し、7つの意味のあるコミットとして整理しました。

## 修正が必要になった背景

- 以前の開発で`gofmt`によるフォーマットチェックが導入されておらず、コードスタイルが統一されていませんでした
- GitHub Actionsワークフローが冗長で、各ワークフローの責務が明確でありませんでした  
- 依存関係の管理が不透明で、直接使用している依存関係が明示されていませんでした
- CI/CDパイプラインに品質チェック（フォーマット、静的解析）が含まれていませんでした

## 実施した変更

### 1. CI/CDワークフロー改善

**新規追加:**
- `quality-check.yml`: コードフォーマット、簡略化、静的解析、依存関係検証を統合

**既存ワークフロー最適化:**
- トリガー条件を`on: [push, pull_request]`に統一
- `go-build.yml`: 冗長なビルドステップを削除、バイナリ機能テストに特化
- `go-test.yml`: `go test -short`で高速テスト実行、`Fast Tests`に改名

### 2. コードフォーマット統一

- `gofmt -s -w .`を全Goファイルに適用
- 19ファイル、233行の挿入・236行の削除による大規模クリーンアップ
- 末尾スペース、インデント不整合、ファイル末尾改行を修正

### 3. 依存関係整理

- 直接依存関係を明示化:
  - `github.com/bluekeyes/go-gitdiff` (パッチ解析)
  - `github.com/go-git/go-git/v5` (テスト用)
- 間接依存関係と直接依存関係を明確に分離
- `go.sum`の段階的な更新で整合性を確保

## 技術的詳細

### セマンティックコミット分割

1858行の大規模パッチを122個のハンクに分析し、`git-sequential-stage`ツールで以下の7つのコミットに分割:

1. `ci: improve workflow configuration and add quality checks`
2. `ci: complete workflow cleanup and optimization` 
3. `style: fix code formatting violations with gofmt`
4. `deps: clarify direct dependencies in go.mod`
5. `deps: update go.sum checksums` (×3回の段階的更新)

### 品質チェック機能

新しい`quality-check.yml`で以下を自動化:
```yaml
- gofmt フォーマットチェック: test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"
- gofmt 簡略化チェック: test -z "$(gofmt -s -l .)"  
- 静的解析: go vet ./...
- 依存関係検証: go mod verify
```

## 検証済み項目

- ✅ 全テストがパス（既存機能に影響なし）
- ✅ コードフォーマットが統一され、今後の`gofmt`チェックをパス
- ✅ 静的解析（`go vet`）でエラーなし
- ✅ 依存関係の整合性確認済み
- ✅ ビルドとバイナリ動作確認済み

## 影響範囲

- **開発効率向上**: CI/CDパイプラインで品質問題を早期発見
- **コード可読性向上**: 統一されたフォーマットでコードレビューが容易に
- **保守性向上**: 明確な依存関係管理と構造化されたワークフロー

body:
Add rate limiting to DPDK packet sender scripts and fix core rate limit application logic.

The existing `--bwl` implementation in `src/init.c` had a bug where `numqueues` was a float, leading to potential inaccuracies, and the rate limit was applied to all possible queues instead of only active ones. This PR corrects the queue counting to `uint32_t` and ensures rate limits are correctly distributed only among active TX queues, making the rate limiting feature reliable.

author: randombit
body:
A long time ago IEEE 1363 was the future of public key cryptography standards, and using their naming schemes seemed helpful. But now 1363 is withdrawn and long since obscure, and nobody knows what an EMSA is.

Fortunately these days the whole concept is hidden and not visible to applications, so it's safe to rename the base type as well as all of the child types.

This retains the terminology in module names and exported feature macros since these are visible to applications. They can be changed in Botan4.

It also enhances the display of images for both products and customers across various views, improving visual representation and user experience.

## 🔧 **Changes Made**

### Core Functionality
- **File Upload API**: Implemented a dedicated Rails API endpoint (`/api/upload`) for secure image uploads, handling validation (type, size) and unique filename generation.
- **Product Image Integration**:
    - Added a modern drag-and-drop image upload interface to the product form with real-time preview and progress indication.
    - Updated product list and detail views to display product images, with a fallback to letter avatars if no image is present.
- **Customer Image Display Enhancement**:
    - Enhanced customer list (table and card) and detail views to display customer images with circular styling, also including a fallback to letter avatars.

### Files Added/Modified
- `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb` - **NEW** File upload API controller
- `app/models/product.rb` - Added image helper methods (`has_image?`, `image_filename`)
- `app/models/customer.rb` - Added image helper methods (`has_image?`, `image_filename`)
- `app/controllers/products_controller.rb` - Permitted `image_url` parameter
- `app/views/products/_form.html.erb` - Added image upload UI and JavaScript
- `app/views/products/index.html.erb` - Updated product image display
- `app/views/products/show.html.erb` - Updated product image display
- `app/views/customers/index.html.erb` - Updated customer image display
- `app/views/customers/show.html.erb` - Updated customer image display
- `config/routes.rb` - Added route for the upload API
- `.gitignore` - Added rules to ignore uploaded files but keep the `uploads` directory
- `public/uploads/.gitkeep` - **NEW** Ensures `uploads` directory is tracked
- `IMAGE_UPLOAD_FEATURE.md` - **NEW** Comprehensive documentation for the feature
- `public/image_upload_demo.html` - **NEW** Standalone demo for image upload functionality

## 🎯 **Business Benefits**

### Product Enhancements
- ✅ **Visual Product Catalogs**: Enables rich visual representation of products, improving user engagement and clarity.
- ✅ **Streamlined Admin Workflow**: Simplifies image management for administrators with an intuitive upload interface.

### Customer Enhancements
- ✅ **Improved Customer Identification**: Provides visual cues for customer profiles in admin views, making it easier to identify individuals.

## 🧪 **Testing**
1.  **Start Rails server**: `rails server`
2.  **Product Image Upload**:
    - Navigate to `Products` -> `New Product` or `Edit` an existing product.
    - Locate the "Product Image" section.
    - Test image upload using both drag & drop and the "Browse Files" button.
    - Verify the image preview, progress bar, and the "Remove Image" functionality.
    - Test with various image types (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP) and sizes (under/over 5MB).
    - Save the product and confirm the image persists.
3.  **Product Image Display**:
    - Navigate to the `Products` index page and verify images are displayed in the list.
    - Click on a product to view its details and confirm the large image is displayed.
    - Verify letter avatar fallback for products without images.
4.  **Customer Image Display**:
    - Navigate to the `Customers` index page (both table and card views) and verify customer images are displayed (if `image_url` is present).
    - Click on a customer to view their details and confirm the image is displayed in the header.
    - Verify letter avatar fallback for customers without images.
5.  **Demo Page**: Access `http://localhost:3000/image_upload_demo.html` to see a standalone demonstration of the upload UI.

## 📚 **Documentation**
- Comprehensive documentation for the image upload feature, including API details, usage instructions, security considerations, and technical aspects, is available in `IMAGE_UPLOAD_FEATURE.md`.

## 🚀 **Deployment Notes**
- These are additive changes only; no existing functionality has been removed or altered in a breaking way.
- A new directory `public/uploads` will be created for storing uploaded images.

## 🔍 **Review Checklist**
- [ ] File upload API security (CSRF protection, file type/size validation) is robust.
- [ ] Image display is consistent and correct across all modified views.
- [ ] Frontend image upload functionality (drag & drop, preview, remove) works as expected.
- [ ] Fallback to letter avatars is correctly implemented for missing images.
- [ ] Code adheres to Rails conventions and best practices.
- [ ] `IMAGE_UPLOAD_FEATURE.md` is accurate and comprehensive.

## 📊 **Impact Assessment**
- **Risk Level**: Low (additive feature, no modification to core business logic).
- **Backward Compatibility**: ✅ Full backward compatibility maintained.
- **Performance Impact**: Minimal (additional HTTP requests for image uploads; image rendering is standard).
- **Database Size**: No significant impact (only image URLs are stored, not binary data).

## 🎉 **Post-Merge Tasks**
1.  Ensure the Rails server is restarted to pick up new routes and controller.
2.  Consider implementing image optimization (e.g., resizing, compression) for production environments to improve performance.
3.  If desired, extend the image upload functionality to customer forms using the same pattern.

body:
# Pull Request Description

## New Resource: aws_wafv2_web_acl_logging_configuration

This PR implements the `aws_wafv2_web_acl_logging_configuration` resource, which allows users to configure logging for AWS WAFv2 Web ACLs. This resource enables customers to:

- Configure log destination configurations for WAFv2 Web ACLs
- Set up logging filters to control what gets logged
- Configure redacted fields to exclude sensitive information from logs

### Implementation Details

The implementation includes:

- Complete resource schema definition with appropriate validation rules
- Full CRUD operations (Create/Put, Read, Update/Put, Delete)
- Helper functions for data transformation between Terraform and AWS API formats
- Support for redacted fields including method, query string, single header, and URI path
- Comprehensive acceptance tests covering various scenarios:
  - Basic resource creation and import
  - Updating single header redacted fields
  - Updating method, query string, and URI path redacted fields
  - Managing multiple redacted fields simultaneously
  - Resource recreation when ARN or log destinations change
  - Proper resource cleanup and disappearance handling
  - Empty redacted fields handling
  - Validation of log destination naming requirements

### Acceptance Test Results

All acceptance tests pass successfully, including:
- Basic resource creation and import
- Various redacted field configurations
- Resource recreation scenarios
- Edge cases and validation tests

### Changelog Entry

```release-note
new resource: aws_wafv2_web_acl_logging_configuration - Provides a resource to manage AWS WAFv2 Web ACL logging configuration
```

### Testing Notes

The implementation has been tested with:
- Various combinations of redacted fields
- Different logging filter configurations
- Resource recreation scenarios
- Import functionality
- Proper error handling for invalid configurations

All tests pass successfully in both regional and global WAFv2 contexts.

### References

- [AWS WAFv2 Logging Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/logging.html)
- [AWS SDK PutLoggingConfiguration API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/APIReference/API_PutLoggingConfiguration.html)

The system adds real-time user behavior tracking, business intelligence dashboards, A/B testing framework, and automated reporting capabilities. **Key Components Added:** - **Analytics Database Schema**: 4 new tables for events, sessions, user analytics, and A/B testing data - **Event Tracking System**: Comprehensive tracking of user actions (assessments, biomarkers, health goals, etc.) - **Analytics Dashboard**: Professional admin interface with key metrics and visualizations - **A/B Testing Framework**: Conversion optimization with variant assignment and tracking - **Automated Processing**: Scheduled data aggregation, cleanup, and report generation - **WordPress Integration**: Admin menus, AJAX handlers, and security implementation **Files Changed:** - `includes/class-advanced-analytics.php` (953 lines) - Complete analytics system implementation - `ADVANCED_ANALYTICS_REPORTING_SUMMARY.md` - Comprehensive documentation ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human ⚠️ **High-Risk Items Requiring Careful Review:** - [ ] **Database Performance Impact** - Review the 4 new analytics tables and frequent INSERT operations. Test with realistic user load to ensure no performance degradation. Verify indexes are properly configured for query performance. - [ ] **Privacy & GDPR Compliance** - Scrutinize IP address collection, user behavior tracking, and data retention policies. Ensure compliance with privacy regulations and consider implementing IP anonymization options. - [ ] **WordPress Security Validation** - Verify all AJAX endpoints have proper nonce verification and permission checks. Test admin menu access controls and ensure analytics data is properly protected from unauthorized access. - [ ] **JavaScript Integration Gap** - Note that this backend expects a client-side JavaScript tracking SDK that wasn't implemented in this PR. The system may not function end-to-end without the frontend tracking code. - [ ] **Data Retention & Cleanup Logic** - Carefully test the automated data cleanup functionality with non-production data. Verify retention settings work correctly and won't accidentally delete important analytics data. **Recommended Testing Plan:** 1. Enable analytics in a staging environment with sample user interactions 2. Verify database tables are created without errors during plugin activation 3. Test admin dashboard loads and displays sample analytics data correctly 4. Validate that tracking doesn't interfere with existing plugin functionality 5. Test data retention cleanup with short retention periods (use test data only!) --- ### Diagram ```mermaid %%{ init : { "theme" : "default" }}%% graph TD A["includes/class-advanced-analytics.php"]:::major-edit B["WordPress Admin Dashboard"]:::context C["Database Tables"]:::major-edit D["User Interactions"]:::context E["JavaScript Tracking SDK"]:::context F["Analytics Reports"]:::major-edit A --> |"Creates & Manages"| C A --> |"Integrates with"| B D --> |"Tracked by"| E E --> |"Sends data to"| A A --> |"Generates"| F C --> |"Stores events, sessions,
user analytics, A/B tests"| A subgraph Legend L1[Major Edit]:::major-edit L2[Minor Edit]:::minor-edit L3[Context/No Edit]:::context end classDef major-edit fill:#90EE90 classDef minor-edit fill:#87CEEB classDef context fill:#FFFFFF ``` ### Notes **Implementation Highlights:** - Comprehensive event tracking for all major plugin features (assessments, biomarkers, health goals) - Professional analytics dashboard with Chart.js visualizations and key performance metrics - A/B testing framework with variant assignment and conversion tracking - Automated data processing with configurable retention policies - WordPress security compliance with nonce verification and permission checks **Known Limitations:** - Client-side JavaScript tracking SDK not implemented in this PR - Analytics dashboard UI is basic HTML structure - may need styling enhancements - Chart.js dependency needs to be properly enqueued in WordPress **Performance Considerations:** - Analytics tracking uses non-blocking AJAX requests to minimize user experience impact - Database queries are optimized with proper indexing strategies - Configurable data retention prevents unlimited database growth --- **Session Details:** - Requested by: ENNU (admin@ennulife.com) - Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/0c5e3f734a884fde9f30d466d8ce66b2

author: copilot
body:
## Problem

The README.md references the `dotnet-install-for-agents` document for .NET installation instructions, but doesn't include the critical warnings about git history pollution that are prominently featured in that document. Users following the installation instructions could accidentally commit temporary files and directories to their project repositories.

## Solution

Applied the same git history guidance that exists in the referenced document to prevent users from polluting project repositories:

### Changes Made

1. **Added prominent warning to README.md** after the reference to dotnet-install-for-agents:
   - Clear warning about not committing downloaded files to git history
   - Specific callout of problematic directories (`_temp/`, `.dotnet/`)
   - Recommended .gitignore patterns with copy-pasteable code block

2. **Updated .gitignore proactively** to include the recommended patterns:
   ```gitignore
   # .NET installation scripts and tools (DO NOT COMMIT)
   _temp/
   
   # .NET SDK installation directory (if installed locally)
   .dotnet/
   ```

### Why This Matters

The dotnet-install-for-agents scripts download temporary files that should never be committed:
- `_temp/` directory contains installation scripts and tools
- `.dotnet/` directory contains SDK installations

Without proper warnings and .gitignore patterns, users could accidentally commit these files, polluting project repositories with build artifacts and temporary installation files.

### Validation

- ✅ Build process unaffected
- ✅ Application functionality unchanged
- ✅ Warning matches style and urgency of referenced document
- ✅ Changes are minimal and surgical

The warning now provides the same level of protection that exists in the referenced document while being tailored to this repository's context.

author: mikhailramalho
body:
In PR #99785, I disabled a test for `epoll_create` that was intended to fail on systems where only `epoll_create1` is available. This is because `epoll_create1` cannot fail in the same way that `epoll_create` does.

Specifically, calling `epoll_create(0)` should result in an EINVAL error. So, when only `epoll_create1` is available, we should simply check if the argument is zero and return the error accordingly.

<!-- Guidelines: https://docs.spacestation14.io/en/getting-started/pr-guideline -->

## About the PR
<!-- What did you change? -->
ConditionalSpawnerSystem.Spawn(Entity<EntityTableSpawnerComponent> ent) now can automatically stack items it spawns if EntityTableSpawnerComponent.AutoStack is set to true.

Requires RT PR to be merged - https://github.com/space-wizards/RobustToolbox/pull/6082

## Why / Balance
<!-- Discuss how this would affect game balance or explain why it was changed. Link any relevant discussions or issues. -->
Fixes #34041 (any problematic spawner should just get 'autoStack: true')

ConditionalSpawnerComponent  is able to spawn more then 1 item, but if it is forced to spawns too many (for example  some game logic decides that it needs 57 sheets of glass) it will just spam them. Better stack them while we can.

## Technical details
<!-- Summary of code changes for easier review. -->
System runs through list of selected prototIds, gets prototypes, seeks its stack component, and groups prototypes by stacks. After aggregation phase it spawns entities and fills stack comp accordingly until every entity that was requested is spawned. Prototypes without StackComponent are processed without any additional logic.

author: plusa2m
body:
Hi everyone,  

I’ve been struggling to efficiently manage translations in my SvelteKit project that uses Paraglide JS—especially when working with tools like Fink and Sherlock. To address this, I decided to create a native macOS app that simplifies the workflow for managing i18n JSON files: **[[i18n Editor](https://github.com/PlusA2M/i18n-editor)](https://github.com/PlusA2M/i18n-editor)**.  

This is my first contribution to the community, and I’m really excited to share it with all of you!  

### Key Features:
- **Native macOS Experience**: A smooth, intuitive interface built with SwiftUI.  
- **Optimized for Paraglide JS**: Automatic detection of `project.inlang/settings.json` and streamlined workflows for SvelteKit projects.  
- **Visual Translation Table**: Spreadsheet-style editing for translations, complete with Excel-like navigation.  
- **Smart Refactoring**: AI-powered suggestions for removing empty keys, merging duplicates, and optimizing structure.  
- **Advanced Search & Validation**: Real-time search across translations, syntax error highlighting, and cross-locale consistency checks.  

### Why This Might Be Useful:  
- Simplifies i18n management for Paraglide JS users.  
- Provides a spreadsheet-like interface to avoid manual JSON editing.  
- Offers built-in validation and refactoring to catch issues before production.  
- Works with any framework that follows the `project.inlang/settings.json` structure.  

I would love for the community to check out the project and share your thoughts. Whether it’s feedback, feature suggestions, or just general impressions, I’m eager to learn and improve!  

**Repo Link**: [[GitHub - PlusA2M/i18n-editor](https://github.com/PlusA2M/i18n-editor)](https://github.com/PlusA2M/i18n-editor)  

Thank you for taking the time to review my work. I hope this app can make translation workflows a little easier for those using Paraglide JS and SvelteKit!  

Looking forward to hearing your feedback! 😊

body:
## Summary
- Completes Docker Hub integration feature (41 SP)
- Adds configurable repository support for custom Docker registries
- Achieves 62-80% size reduction compared to original images

## Changes
### 🗑️ Removed Old Bloated Images
- Removed fastapi/Dockerfile (1.3GB)
- Removed nextjs/Dockerfile (1.41GB)
- Removed python-dev/Dockerfile

### ✨ Added Optimized Base Images
- Python base: 495MB (62% smaller) with UV package manager
- Node.js base: 276MB (80% smaller) with npm
- Both include development tools and Oh My Zsh

### ⚙️ Configurable Repository Support
- Users can specify custom Docker registries in `~/.spinbox/global.conf`
- Support for private registries and custom image names
- Maintains backward compatibility with default images

### 📚 Documentation
- Comprehensive user guide for Docker Hub configuration
- Updated implementation plan showing completion
- Added future enhancements to backlog

## Test Results
All tests passing ✅ (ran comprehensive testing with complex scenarios)

## Performance Impact
- 50-70% faster project creation when using `--docker-hub` flag
- Graceful fallback to local builds when Docker Hub unavailable

## 작업 내용 요약 Closes #33 - 작성자 신고 API 및 테스트 추가 - 작성자 차단 API 및 테스트 추가 - 둘다 로직은 동일합니다. ### 리뷰해주면 좋겠는 점 1. DataInitializer에 들어가긴 부적합하다고 생각하는 테스트 데이터를 넣는 방식 ```java @Test @DisplayName("회원을 차단한다") void blockTest() { // given databaseInitializer.setUserInfo(); memberCommandService.signup(new SignupRequest("user2", "https://user2.png", "user2@gmail.com")); //이부분 주목 -> 회원이 차단을 할 대상 회원을 데이터베이스에 추가한다. 다만 범용적으로 사용하는 데이터는 아니어서 databaseInitializer에 메서드를 추가하진 않았다. String token = MemberFixture.login("user@gmail.com"); // when - then ... ``` 위와 같이 **한두개의 테스트 시나리오를 위한 데이터**가 필요할 때, 어떤 방식으로 추가하는게 좋을지? 저는 DatabaseInitializer는 모든 테스트에서 범용적으로 쓸만한 정도의 데이터만 넣어두는 거라고 생각해, 이경우엔 DatabaseInitializer를 사용하지 않았어요. 지금은 일단 쉽게쉽게 memberCommandService를 불러와서 추가했습니다. 다른 의견 있으면 리뷰 부탁~~ 2. Member 패키지 안에 신고와 차단로직을 두었습니다. 더 좋은 구조가 있다면 제시해주세요! ## 충돌 주의! - DatabaseInitializer의 메서드 시그니처가 변경되면서 여러 테스트 메서드에서 conflict가 날 수 있습니다. 변경된 사항에 맞춰서 수정해주시면 돼요! --- ## 리뷰/머지 희망 기한 (선택) - 내일 (21일) 13시 전! --- ## 셀프 체크리스트 - [x] 프로그램이 정상적으로 작동하는가? - [x] 모든 테스트가 통과하는가? - [x] 불필요한 주석 또는 디버깅을 위한 Log를 모두 제거하였는가? - [x] 코딩 스타일 가이드를 준수하였는가? - [x] IDE 코드 자동 정렬을 적용하였는가?
📖 효과적인 코드 리뷰를 위한 제안 ## 1. 작업 목표 설정 ### 목표 명확화 - 이슈 티켓 발행 시 이슈의 목표를 명확히 설정한다 - 큰 작업은 여러 개의 작은 티켓으로 분할하여 진행한다 - **PR은 최대 500 Line 제한** - 주요 변경사항이나 새로운 패턴 도입 시 **반드시 사전에 논의**한다 ## 2. 마감 기한 설정 - 리뷰 및 반영 기간이 길어질수록 PR의 크기는 커진다 - 리뷰에 대한 부담을 줄이기 위해 **피드백 마감기한을 팀과 설정** - **리뷰 완료 기준 24시간 이내** ## 3. 리뷰어의 자세와 원칙 ### 3.1 기본 원칙 - 피드백은 **코드, 프로세스, 사양만**을 대상으로 한다 - 리뷰이와 리뷰어의 인격과는 **분리**되어야 한다 - 언어 폭력이나 비난이 섞인 지적은 리뷰가 아니다 - **시간에 쫓겨 리뷰의 품질을 낮추지 말자** ### 3.2 리뷰어의 자세 - **리뷰는 모두를 위한 것이다**: 나 자신과 팀, 서비스를 위한 것. 새로 감정이 상하지 않도록 노력이 필요 - **적절한 시간 분배**: 리뷰어가 감당할 수 있는 양의 리뷰를 나누고, 피드백 마감기한을 지키자 - **우선순위를 정해 피드백이 필요한 부분만 간단히 리뷰를 주고받는다** ### 3.3 리뷰 의견 제시 방법 #### 건설적 피드백 - **긍정적 표현 사용** - ❌ "이 코드는 잘못되었다" - ✅ "이 부분을 다음과 같이 개선할 수 있을 것 같습니다" #### 구체적인 제안 - ❌ "성능이 안 좋다" - ✅ "A 방법 대신 B를 사용하면 가독성이 향상될 것 같습니다" #### 리뷰는 토론과 같다 - 토론을 하되, 리뷰를 넘길 때도 의견과 함께 리뷰어가 납득할 수 있는 이유와 근거(자료 등)를 충분히 제시 ### 3.4 적절한 시간 분배 - 리뷰를 위한 리뷰는 리뷰 품질의 저하을 초래한다. 피드백 할 부분이 없다면 **칭찬을 남기자** - 사람은 누구나 실수한다 - **리뷰어, 리뷰어 모두 실수를 빠르게 인정하고 열린 마음으로 토론하는 것이 중요** - 실수를 지적받았을 때 **방어적이 되지 않는다** --- ## 효과적인 코드 리뷰를 위한 마인드셋 - **리뷰는 모두를 위한 것이다**: 나 자신과 팀, 서비스를 위한 것 - **사람은 누구나 실수한다**: 리뷰어, 리뷰어 모두 실수를 빠르게 인정하고 열린 마음으로 토론하는 것이 중요 - **칭찬도 좋은 코드 리뷰이다**: 특별히 남길 의견이 없다면 칭찬을 해보자 ### 리뷰를 위한 리뷰 자제 - 리뷰를 위한 리뷰는 자제하자. 리뷰를 위한 리뷰는 지적을 초래한다 ---

body:
This pull request introduces Grafana Faro for frontend observability, including SDK integration, environment variable configuration, and documentation updates. The changes enhance the application's ability to track performance metrics, errors, and user interactions, while providing detailed instructions for setup and usage.

### Grafana Faro Integration

* **Environment Variable Configuration**: Added new variables in `.env.example` for Grafana Faro setup, including `VITE_GRAFANA_FARO_URL`, `VITE_GRAFANA_FARO_API_KEY`, and others for telemetry and source map uploads.
* **SDK Initialization**: Implemented `initializeFaroSDK` in `src/lib/faro.ts` to configure Grafana Faro with React integration, session tracking, and web instrumentation.
* **Page Tracking**: Added `useFaroPageTracking` hook in `src/lib/faroPageTracking.ts` for custom page view analytics, including multilingual support and route tracking.

### Documentation Updates

* **New Documentation**: Added `GRAFANA_FARO.md` in both English (`docs/en/`) and Spanish (`docs/es/`) to guide users through Grafana Faro setup and usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-706c720d58cab37e4aed01a9a15c879f7c9e3eb10bb89bb1b7d7048cec07d6dbR1-R209) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-870216143b481569eac9caac03a974abc9428707f534ccb7d31c54ad3c9dda33R1-R242)

### Application Enhancements

* **Page View Logging**: Integrated `useFaroPageTracking` into `src/components/Layout.tsx` for automatic page view tracking. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a4d72ac54801a218d7cfd27d169a7724d8c041bba5f6ba18e501670faab655a4R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a4d72ac54801a218d7cfd27d169a7724d8c041bba5f6ba18e501670faab655a4R47-R48)

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the complete initial setup for the nntp-rs client library as requested in the issue. The library follows a modern sans-io design pattern with optional async runtime integrations.

## Key Features

### Sans-IO Design
- **Protocol Logic Separation**: Core NNTP protocol implementation is completely separated from I/O operations
- **Runtime Agnostic**: Can be used with any async runtime or custom I/O implementation
- **Flexible Integration**: Allows users to provide their own networking layer while leveraging the protocol implementation

### NNTP Protocol Support
- Complete command encoding for all major NNTP commands (CAPABILITIES, GROUP, ARTICLE, etc.)
- Robust response parsing with proper error handling
- Type-safe API with comprehensive error types
- State management for connection lifecycle

### Async Runtime Integrations
Optional feature-gated integrations for popular async runtimes:
- `tokio-runtime` - Tokio integration with high-level client
- `async-std-runtime` - async-std integration  
- `smol-runtime` - smol runtime integration
- `all-runtimes` - Convenience feature for all runtimes

### Example Usage

```rust
// Sans-IO usage (manual I/O handling)
use nntp_rs::{Client, Command};

let mut client = Client::new();
let request = client.encode_command(Command::Capabilities)?;
// Send request through your I/O layer...

// High-level Tokio usage
use nntp_rs::tokio::NntpClient;

let mut client = NntpClient::connect("news.example.com:119").await?;
let capabilities = client.capabilities().await?;
```

## Development Infrastructure

### Comprehensive CI/CD
- GitHub Actions workflow with cargo caching
- Multi-version Rust testing (stable, beta, nightly)
- Feature matrix testing for all runtime combinations
- Code formatting, linting, and documentation checks
- Code coverage reporting
- MSRV (Minimum Supported Rust Version) validation

### Quality Assurance
- **17 unit tests** covering core functionality
- **5 doc tests** ensuring example code works
- **Clippy compliance** with strict warning settings
- **rustfmt** formatting consistency
- Comprehensive documentation with examples

### Library Structure
```
src/
├── lib.rs          # Main library interface
├── client.rs       # Sans-io client implementation  
├── command.rs      # NNTP command types and encoding
├── response.rs     # NNTP response types and parsing
├── error.rs        # Error types and handling
├── tokio.rs        # Tokio integration
├── async_std.rs    # async-std integration
└── smol.rs         # smol integration
```

## Testing

All tests pass with various feature combinations:
```bash
cargo test                           # Sans-io only
cargo test --features tokio-runtime  # With Tokio
cargo test --all-features           # All runtimes
```

The library is ready for immediate use and follows Rust best practices for API design, documentation, and testing.

Fixes #1.

author: justin-millman
body:
This commit hardens the translation logic regarding nullability and Relations. In particular:

   * Relations cannot be natively nullable
   * Natively nullable Relations that are annotated as [NonNullable] are supported
   * The element of an unordered list- or set-like Relation cannot be natively nullable
   * The key of a map-like Relation cannot be natively nullable

A few unit tests have been tweaked, and a handle of additional tests have been written. A new exception type has been added to indicate when something is impermissibily natively nullable.

author: drovani
body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive skeleton loading components throughout the Hero Wars Helper application to improve perceived performance and user experience. This addresses **GitHub Issue #61** by replacing basic loading spinners with contextual skeleton placeholders that match final content layouts.

**Key Achievement**: Created a complete skeleton loading infrastructure with 13 specialized components covering all major application areas.

## Implementation Details

### 🏗️ Core Infrastructure (5 Components)
- **`SkeletonCard`** - Configurable card-based content placeholders with size variants
- **`SkeletonTable`** - Table layouts with rows, columns, and action areas
- **`SkeletonForm`** - Form fields, sections, and button placeholders
- **`SkeletonGrid`** - Responsive grid layouts with configurable item counts

## Summary

This PR addresses code quality improvements for the Windows MTR project, resolving compiler warnings, enhancing documentation, and updating dependencies to their latest stable versions.

## Changes Made

### 🔧 Compiler Warning Fixes
- **Fixed useless comparison warning**: Removed redundant port validation check for `port > 65535` since `u16` type already enforces this constraint
- **Improved port validation**: Now properly validates against port 0 (invalid) while leveraging type system for upper bound

```rust
// Before: Useless comparison (u16 can't exceed 65535)
if port > 65535 {
    return Err(MtrError::InvalidOption(format!("Port number {} is out of range", port)));
}

// After: Meaningful validation
if port == 0 {
    return Err(MtrError::InvalidOption(format!("Port number {port} is invalid (must be 1-65535)")));
}
```

### 🎨 Clippy Lint Improvements
- **Eliminated redundant closures**: Simplified error handling by using function references directly
- **Enhanced format strings**: Replaced placeholder format strings with inline variables for better readability
- **Improved code efficiency**: Applied Rust best practices for cleaner, more maintainable code

### 📚 Documentation Enhancements
Added comprehensive inline documentation for key functions:

- **`find_trippy_binary()`**: Documents the binary location search strategy and fallback logic
- **`validate_target()`**: Explains hostname resolution and IP address validation approach  
- **`verify_options()`**: Details command-line option validation and error handling

### 📦 Dependency Updates
- **Updated `clap`**: Bumped from `4.5.37` to `4.5.41` for latest security fixes and improvements
- **Maintained compatibility**: All existing functionality preserved with enhanced stability

### 🧪 Test Coverage Improvements
- **Added port validation tests**: New test cases verify handling of valid port ranges (1, 443, 65535)
- **Enhanced edge case coverage**: Ensures robust validation of port number boundaries
- **Increased test count**: From 7 to 8 passing tests

## Validation

- ✅ **All tests pass**: 8 tests passing, 2 appropriately ignored (network-dependent)
- ✅ **Clean compilation**: No compiler warnings or clippy lints
- ✅ **Release build**: Optimized release binary builds successfully
- ✅ **Backward compatibility**: All existing functionality preserved

## Technical Details

The changes maintain full backward compatibility while improving code quality and maintainability. The fixes address static analysis recommendations and follow Rust best practices for error handling and documentation.

**Before**: 1 compiler warning, 4 clippy warnings  
**After**: 0 warnings, enhanced documentation, improved test coverage

These improvements enhance the codebase quality without altering any user-facing functionality or breaking existing workflows.

body:
Adds a tool called `cargo stack-size` which can used installed via `cargo install` for easily inspecting stack sizes of a binary by function or crate. Please see the `README` for more information.

If you would like to test it before merged, it can be installed via:
`cargo install --git https://github.com/kurtjd/odp-utilities --branch cargo-stack-size cargo-stack-size`

and then used as described in the `README`.

The clippy lint levels have been switched to `deny` as unfortunately `forbid` is too restrictive and doesn't even allow dependencies to override the lint level, which `clap` does.

**Edit**: Appears to be failing some CI checks for requiring `rustc 1.86` which is greater than MSRV, and for not passing `cargo deny`. However as this is a binary crate and not a library, I feel these don't apply. May move this to a different repo.

author: dandavison
body:
Implements cancellation types for Python Nexus. This PR is mainly tests. These provide coverage for the state machine changes in https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-core/pull/977. See https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-core/issues/911#issuecomment-3151904819


The gist for anyone who needs a refresher is:

- `Abandon` - caller workflow never even sends a request cancel command. The state machine is such that the operation handle future is resolved with a cancellation exception in a second activation in the same WFT

- `TryCancel` - same as `Abandon` regarding the immediate resolution of the future, but do emit the cancel nexus op request command (maybe it could also have been called RequestAsync or something)

For the next two, one has to keep two concepts clearly distinct: the Nexus cancel handler invocation, and cancellation of the nexus op itself. The typical case is that the handler issues a `RequestCancelWorkflowExecution` to the workflow that's backing the nexus operation and then when that workflow is eventually cancelled, that triggers cancellation of the nexus op itself (the worfklow  reaching a terminal state triggers some nexus stuff server-side)

- `WaitRequested` - caller workflow issues the cancel request command, and waits for an event saying that the cancel handler invocation is complete (that event is the new event for which Rust state machine changes were made)

- `WaitCompleted` - caller workflow issues the cancel request command and waits for the operation to be cancelled (isn't affected by the new event)

And then finally, it's not one new event; there's two because the cancel handler might succeed or fail. Under `WaitRequested` the fail event also resolves the nexus operation handle future in the caller workflow, but as a normal nexus error, not as cancelled.

author: cepawiel
body:
Vimin VM-S100-0800MS is an 8 port Multi-Gig switch, based on RTL9303. Ported from XikeStor SKS8300-8X with changes to support different u-boot build.

Specification:

- SoC             : Realtek RTL9303
- RAM             : DDR3 512 MiB
- Flash           :  SPI-NOR 16 MiB (Winbond W25Q128JVSQ)
- Ethernet        : 8x 1/2.5/10 Gbps (SFP+)
- LEDs/Keys (GPIO): 0x/1x
- UART            : "Console" port on the front panel
  - type          : RS-232C
  - connector     : RJ-45
  - settings      : 115200n8
- Power           : AC100-240V 50/60Hz

Flash instruction using initramfs image:

 1. Prepare TFTP server with an IP address "192.168.1.111"
 2. Connect your PC to Port1 on VM-S100-0800MS
 3. Power on VM-S100-0800MS and interrupt boot by pressing Esc
 4. Enable Port1 with the following commands

    rtk 10g 0 fiber1g (or fiber10g if 10GBase-*R, dac300cm for DAC cable) rtk ext-devInit 0 rtk ext-pinSet 2 0

    Note: the last command sets tx-disable to low

 7. Download initramfs image from TFTP server

    tftpboot 0x82000000 <image name>

 8. Boot with the downloaded image

    bootm

 9. On the initramfs image, backup the stock firmware if needed
10. Upload (or download) sysupgrade image to the device
11. Erase "firmware" partition to cleanup JFFS2 of stock FW

    mtd erase firmware

12. Perform sysupgrade with the sysupgrade image
13. Wait ~120 sec to complete flashing

Reverting to stock firmware:
 1. Prepare by downloading the stock firmware. Vimin doesn't have the firmware on their website, tested using firmware for shared hardware Nicgiga S100-0800S-M. Filename: vmlinux-nicgiga-S100-0800S-M-241126EN.bix

 2. Prepare TFTP server with an IP address "192.168.1.111"
 3. Connect your PC to Port1 on VM-S100-0800MS
 4. Power on VM-S100-0800MS and interrupt boot by pressing Esc
 5. Enable Port1 with the following commands

    rtk 10g 0 fiber1g (or fiber10g if 10GBase-*R, dac300cm for DAC cable) rtk ext-devInit 0 rtk ext-pinSet 2 0

    Note: the last command sets tx-disable to low

 6. Download initramfs image from TFTP server

    tftpboot 0x82000000 <image name>

 7. Boot with the downloaded image

    bootm

 8. Under Management -> Firmware -> Upgrade/Backup, upload bix file.
 9. Reboot device

author: lawsonstation
body:
Implementation of the following opcodes:
| Instruction code (hex) | Instruction mnemonic | Description                                                 |
| ---------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| 00                     | NOP                  | No-operation                                                |
| 01                     | LXI B,d16            | Load immediate register pair B & C                          |
| 11                     | LXI D,d16            | Load Register Pair D and E Immediate 16-bit Data            |
| 21                     | LXI H,d16            | Load Register Pair H and L Immediate 16-bit Data            |
| 31                     | LXI SP,d16           | Load Stack Pointer Immediate 16-bit Data                    |
| 5E                     | MOV E,M              | Move Data from Memory (addressed by H and L) to Register E  |
| 7A                     | MOV A,D              | Move Data from Register D to Accumulator                    |
| 7E                     | MOV A,M              | Move Data from Memory (addressed by H and L) to Accumulator |
| C3                     | JMP a16              | Jump Direct                                                 |
| CD                     | CALL a16             | Call Subroutine Direct                                      |
| E1                     | POP H                | Pop register pair H & L off stack                           |
| F1                     | POP PSW              | Pop A and Flags off stack                                   |
| FE                     | CPI d8               | Compare Immediate 8-bit Data with Accumulator               |

Note that opcodes' logic is implemented but pending testing. Some opcodes were merged in an earlier commit (refer to https://github.com/au-gold/CS467_Emulator/commit/b2ac2a132fe0a09f627eac3844267f37ff208bb2).

author: micheljung
body:
My idea is to connect a Lua table to an Actor, but without "mixing" them.

So `UShipLuaComponent::LuaObject` references the Lua table:
```cpp
/** The Lua table that is connected to this actor component. */
FLuaValue LuaObject;
```

When the actor is spawned, a Lua table should be created for it:
```cpp
void UShipLuaComponent::BeginPlay()
{
  Super::BeginPlay();

  const TArray Args = {FLuaValue(this)};
  LuaObject = LuaCallFunction("Ship.Init", Args, true);
}
```
```lua
--- This function is called by the engine whenever a [Ship] actor is spawned.
---@param actor ShipActor the engine actor that is connected to this table
function Ship.Init(actor)
  local instance = setmetatable({}, Ship)
  instance.Actor = actor
  return instance
end
```

The reason I do this is because modders should be able to add functions to `Ship`:
```lua
-- HasTarget should not have to exist in the LuaComponent
function Ship:HasTarget()
  return self.Target ~= nil
end
```
But they can also delegate to the `LuaComponent`:
```lua
---@param input number Value from `0.0` - `1.0`
function Ship:SetThrottleInput(input)
  self.Actor.SetThrottleInput(input)
end
```

And when the engine calls a function like `Tick`, `self` should be the Lua table, not the `LuaComponent`:
```lua
function Ship:Tick(deltaTime)
  print("Tick "..deltaTime)
end
```

To achieve this, I need to be able to call a Lua function without passing the `LuaComponent` implicitly as `self`. I thought that the setting `bImplicitSelf = false` would achieve this. But in methods like `LuaCallFunction`, this flag is not respected.

This PR fixes that.

Unfortunately, this is a breaking change. To preserve the old behavior, `bImplicitSelf` would need to default to `true`, but that would also be a breaking change.

Maybe I'm not getting it right anyway. In that case, maybe a new flag could be introduced to control the behavior? Then it would also not be breaking.

author: tomabadie
body:
## Feature: Filter Recipes by Average User Rating

This PR introduces a new filter for searching recipes based on their **average user rating**.

### Key Changes

* [x] Updated the database to include user ratings for existing recipes, enabling testing and validation.
* [x] Updated the previous dynamic SQL query to filter by the average user rating.
* [x] Enabled counting the total number of filtered recipes using a simplified subquery-based SQL structure.
* [x] Added conditional rendering to **hide pagination and navigation buttons** when no recipes match the search criteria.
* [x] Added comments in `recipesRepository.tsx` to clarify SQL logic and improve code readability.

### Notes

* The database now includes ratings from the three pre-existing users for better testing coverage.
* Filtering by user rating now works together with other existing filters (name, price, duration, eco score).
* This feature improves UX by avoiding unnecessary pagination elements when no results are available.

### Next Steps (mentionned in a previous PR)

* [ ] Add a loading spinner to improve UI responsiveness.
* [ ]  Replace native checkboxes and radios with custom SVG components for better styling control.
* [ ]  Enable navigation back to the filtered recipe list with state preservation.

author: rishabsingh3003
body:
Allow  sending position targets by PrecLand library as position estimates for the vehicle.
 
The advantage of doing this inside PrecLand library is:
1. Works with existing IR-Lock/Aruco Marker type setups with no changes
2. Allows GPS-Denied/GPS-Degraded landing 
3. User could use the new EK3_OPTIONS bit to have one lane running GPS and another lane running "PrecLand" position source. This way they could monitor the innovations/other metrics and see which source they want to use as primary to land. 

While using the PrecLand library isn't necessarily the best way to achieve this because we don't have a good way to send in covariances etc from the sensor,  but it is good for integrating in systems which already use a precland system.

This has been tested in SITL and real vehicle as part of larger work. More testing to follow

O path `'sounds/error_beep.wav'` estava hardcoded no código, mas o arquivo atual é `error_beep.txt`. Esta mudança introduz uma constante para o path e corrige a extensão do arquivo.

## Mudanças implementadas

- ✅ Adicionada constante `static const String _errorSoundPath = 'sounds/error_beep.txt'` na classe `SshProvider`
- ✅ Substituído o path hardcoded `'sounds/error_beep.wav'` pela constante `_errorSoundPath` na função `_playErrorSound()`
- ✅ Corrigida a extensão do arquivo (.wav → .txt) para corresponder ao arquivo existente
- ✅ Adicionados testes para verificar a funcionalidade de configuração de som de erro

## Código antes
```dart
_audioPlayer.play(AssetSource('sounds/error_beep.wav')).catchError((e) {
```

## Código depois
```dart
static const String _errorSoundPath = 'sounds/error_beep.txt';
// ...
_audioPlayer.play(AssetSource(_errorSoundPath)).catchError((e) {
```

## Arquivos modificados
- `lib/providers/ssh_provider.dart` - Adicionada constante e substituído path hardcoded
- `test/providers/ssh_provider_test.dart` - Adicionados testes para funcionalidade de som

Esta implementação segue o padrão já existente no projeto de usar constantes estáticas (como em `error_handler.dart` e `secure_storage_service.dart`) e garante que o path do arquivo esteja correto e centralizadamente gerenciado.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete prototype for intelligent song structure segmentation in the Python backend, replacing the basic placeholder implementation with advanced Music Information Retrieval (MIR) techniques.

## Key Features Implemented

### 🎵 Advanced Segmentation Algorithm
- **Frame-based boundary detection** using chroma, RMS energy, and spectral centroid features
- **Sliding window analysis** with 5-second windows to detect significant musical changes
- **Intelligent section labeling** with position-aware heuristics and confidence scores
- **Robust fallback** handling for edge cases and challenging audio

### 📊 Enhanced Analysis Output
The segmentation now provides:
- **Multiple section types**: Intro, Verse, Chorus, Bridge, Outro
- **Confidence scores** (0.0-1.0) for each detected section
- **Precise timing** with ~0.09s resolution using 2048-sample hop length
- **Reasonable boundaries** with minimum 12-second section constraint

### 🧪 Comprehensive Testing
- Added `test_segmentation.py` with synthetic audio validation
- Tests algorithm accuracy against known section boundaries
- Validates reasonable section count and label diversity
- Demonstrates high confidence scores (>0.9) and accurate boundary detection

## Technical Implementation

The algorithm works by:
1. Extracting musical features (chroma for harmony, RMS for energy, spectral centroid for brightness)
2. Using sliding window comparison to detect significant feature changes
3. Applying combined scoring (chroma + energy×5 + brightness/1000) for boundary strength
4. Labeling sections based on song position, energy levels, and harmonic characteristics

## Test Results

Validated with synthetic audio containing known boundaries:
- **Expected**: 0s, 10s, 25s, 40s, 50s, 60s
- **Detected**: 0s, 12.7s, 26.4s, 40.0s, 53.7s, 60s
- **Accuracy**: Within 2-3 seconds of expected boundaries
- **Confidence**: 0.91-0.99 for all sections

## Before/After Comparison

**Before**: Simple placeholder dividing songs into 4 equal parts with static labels
```
Intro: 0-22.5s, Verse: 22.5-45s, Chorus: 45-67.5s, Outro: 67.5-90s
```

**After**: Intelligent MIR-based detection with confidence scores
```
Intro: 0-12.72s (confidence: 0.92)
Verse 2: 12.72-26.38s (confidence: 0.93)  
Chorus: 26.38-40.03s (confidence: 0.93)
Verse: 40.03-53.68s (confidence: 0.91)
Outro: 53.68-60s (confidence: 0.99)
```

## Documentation Updates
- Enhanced docstrings with detailed algorithm explanation
- Updated README with advanced features and usage examples
- Added comprehensive test suite documentation

Fixes #7.

**Reverse Linked List Challenge**
I reversed a singly linked list using an iterative approach. 

**3Sum Challenge**
My approach uses the two-pointer technique after first sorting the array.

**Merge Two Sorted Lists**
I wrote a function that uses a dummy node and a pointer current to build a new sorted list by comparing values.

**Product of Array Except Self**
I used an approach involving two passes over the array.

**String Encode and Decode**
I wrote a function that encodes by prefixing each string with its length, followed by (#).

**Top K Frequent Elements**
I used a dictionary to count how often each number appears, sorted, extracted, and returned the first k elements.

### Something I learnt

**Reverse Linked List Challenge**
- How to manually reverse a linked list by manipulating next pointers.
- How to write and test linked list problems without using a class-based approach.

**3Sum Challenge**

- Handling duplicates correctly.

author: zetavg
body:
## Problem

When running `backend/dev.sh` + `npm run dev`, developers encounter:
  - Frontend displays: "Oops! You're using an unsupported method (frontend
  only). Please serve the WebUI from the backend."
  - Browser console shows CORS error for `http://localhost:8080/api/config`

## Root Cause

The `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN` in `backend/dev.sh` seems to have a trailing slash that doesn't match browser requests:
  - Configured: `http://localhost:5173/` (with slash)
  - Browser sends: `http://localhost:5173` (no slash)

This mismatch causes CORS rejection, preventing the frontend from fetching APIs.

## Solution

Remove the trailing slash from `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN` to match browser behavior.

I'm not entirely sure I understand everything correctly though. Maybe I've done something wrong that has led to this issue.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements robust drag-and-drop and file picker functionality for audio files in the SwiftUI frontend, addressing the core requirement to allow users to load audio files for analysis.

## Key Features Implemented

### 🎯 Drag-and-Drop Support
- **Visual feedback**: Dynamic border styling and animations when dragging files over the drop zone
- **File validation**: Accepts only valid audio file formats with proper error handling
- **Supported formats**: MP3, WAV, AIFF, AIF, M4A, FLAC, OGG, WMA, AAC, OPUS
- **Format indicators**: Visual badges showing supported file types (MP3, WAV, M4A, FLAC)

### 📁 File Picker Integration  
- **Native macOS dialog**: Uses system file picker with audio file filtering
- **Security compliance**: Proper handling of security-scoped resources for sandboxed apps
- **Error handling**: User-friendly error alerts for file selection failures

### 🎨 Enhanced User Experience
- **Clear functionality**: Added "Clear" button with confirmation dialog to remove current file
- **Smooth animations**: Polished transitions for drag states and UI interactions
- **Professional styling**: Follows macOS Human Interface Guidelines
- **Comprehensive error handling**: Graceful handling of edge cases and invalid files

## Technical Improvements

### Fixed Compilation Issues
- Resolved scope issues with `isShowingFilePicker` binding across components
- Added proper parameter passing between `ContentView`, `AudioFileInfoView`, and `AudioFileDropView`

### Enhanced Implementation
- Improved `onDrop` handler to properly handle `UTType.fileURL` in addition to `UTType.audio`
- Added `isValidAudioFile()` helper function for robust file validation
- Implemented `url.startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()` for proper macOS sandboxing support

### UI/UX Enhancements
- Added `isTargeted` state with animations for visual drag feedback
- Enhanced drop zone styling with dynamic border effects
- Added format badge indicators for better user guidance
- Implemented confirmation dialogs for destructive actions

## Code Structure
The implementation maintains clean separation of concerns:
- `ContentView`: Main container with state management and file picker integration
- `AudioFileDropView`: Dedicated drag-and-drop handling with visual feedback
- `AudioFileInfoView`: File display and management controls

## Testing Scenarios Covered
- ✅ Drag various audio formats from Finder
- ✅ File picker functionality with different file locations  
- ✅ Invalid file type rejection with user feedback
- ✅ Clear/reset functionality with confirmation
- ✅ Visual feedback during drag operations
- ✅ Error handling for file access issues

The implementation provides a robust, user-friendly way to load audio files that integrates seamlessly with the existing analysis pipeline and follows native macOS conventions.

Fixes #12.

## What?
Migrate JUCX publishing from OSSRH to Central Portal to fix Maven deployment failures.

## Why?
OSSRH reached End-of-Life on June 30, 2025: https://central.sonatype.org/pages/ossrh-eol/
All namespaces were migrated to Central Portal, requiring updated build configuration to use the new publishing system.

## How?
- Use `nexus-staging-maven-plugin` with Central Portal compatibility endpoints
- Update distribution management URLs to `ossrh-staging-api.central.sonatype.com`
- Configure pipeline to use `central` server ID in settings.xml

## Summary

Adds comprehensive branch management guidelines to CLAUDE.md based on lessons learned from recent conflict resolution in PR #26.

### Documentation Added

- **Branch Creation Best Practices**: Requirements for fresh branches from `origin/master`
- **Step-by-Step Workflow**: Complete git commands for proper branch management
- **Conflict Prevention**: Explains why starting from updated master reduces conflicts
- **Common Pitfalls**: Lists mistakes to avoid when creating branches

### Why This Matters

This documentation addresses real issues encountered during development:
- Prevents merge conflicts like those in PR #26
- Ensures clean, reviewable commit history
- Provides consistent workflow for all contributors
- Reduces time spent resolving conflicts

### Key Guidelines

✅ **Always start from latest `origin/master`**
✅ **Sync local master before creating branches** 
✅ **Use proper branch naming conventions**
✅ **Rebase instead of merge when conflicts arise**

### Recommended Workflow

```bash
# 1. Switch to master and sync with origin
git checkout master
git pull origin master

# 2. Create new feature branch immediately
git checkout -b feat/your-feature-name

# 3. Work on your feature
# 4. Rebase before PR if needed
# 5. Push and create PR
```

author: ashmod
body:
## TLDR

Adds the ability for users to press **CTRL+A** during the OAuth authentication code entry to clear their previously selected authentication method and restart the CLI for new authentication.

This would make it easier for users on the authentication screen (specifically Google Login method) to go back and choose another authentication method without having to clear the configuration files manually.

## Dive Deeper

1. During OAuth code entry, user presses **CTRL+A** if they need to pick another authentication method
2. CLI clears cached credentials and resets the selected auth method
3. CLI automatically restarts and shows the auth selection dialog again
4. User can choose a different authentication method

### Files Changed

- **`packages/cli/index.ts`**: Added exit code handling for auth clearing
- **`packages/cli/src/gemini.tsx`**: Added error handling to clear settings when auth is reset
- **`packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts`**: Added "CTRL+A" hotkey detection in OAuth flow
- **`scripts/start.js`**: Added restart logic when auth is cleared


### Related Issues
- Fixes [4089](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/4089)
- Related to [1432](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/1432)
- Related to [2547](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/2547)

author: veskoap
body:
This pull request introduces several enhancements to the project, including the addition of CI workflows, testing and coverage setup, debugging endpoints, and Sentry profiling. These changes improve the development process, testing capabilities, and system observability.

### CI and Coverage Enhancements:
* Added a new `.github/workflows/test.yml` workflow for running tests on `main` and `develop` branches, including type checking and dependency installation.
* Introduced a `.github/workflows/test-coverage.yml` workflow to generate and upload test coverage reports to Codecov, with weekly scheduled runs.
* Configured `.codecov.yml` to enforce coverage thresholds, set precision, and define notification behavior.

### Documentation Updates:
* Added `TESTING.md` to provide a comprehensive guide for setting up, running, and troubleshooting tests, including details on Codecov integration and best practices.
* Created `SENTRY_PROFILING.md` to document the setup and usage of Sentry profiling for performance monitoring on both server and client sides.

### Debugging Endpoints:
* Implemented a `GET` endpoint in `app/api/debug/paddle-config/route.ts` to validate Paddle configuration, enforce access control, and provide debugging instructions.
* Added a `POST` endpoint in `app/api/debug/test-webhook/route.ts` to emit test webhook events for debugging real-time notifications and SSE connections.
* Developed a `POST` endpoint in `app/api/debug/update-assistant-webhook/route.ts` to update assistant webhook configurations with environment-based settings.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Introduced a modernized Paddle payment and subscription system, including inline checkout, transaction history, and subscription management.
  * Added secure, user-scoped APIs for managing Paddle transactions, user settings, and VAPI assistants.
  * Implemented Sentry performance profiling and enhanced error monitoring across the app.
  * Added comprehensive test infrastructure with Jest and Testing Library, including code coverage reporting.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed subscription lifecycle handling to ensure immediate dashboard lockout on cancellation or expiration.
  * Resolved webhook processing issues and improved user lookup logic for robust subscription updates.

* **Security**
  * Added strict runtime safeguards and layered security for admin functions, preventing client-side misuse and enforcing server-only execution.
  * Enhanced input validation and safe URL construction to prevent SSRF and injection attacks.

* **Documentation**
  * Expanded and updated documentation for billing, security architecture, testing, and system patterns.

* **Chores**
  * Updated dependencies, added new scripts, and integrated CI workflows for testing and coverage.
  * Improved environment variable validation and configuration debugging endpoints.

author: spencerduncan
body:
## Summary
Implements a builder pattern for `ProcessingContext` to improve usability and provide a more fluent API for configuration, addressing issue #212.

## Changes
- ✅ Added `ProcessingContextBuilder` struct with fluent API
- ✅ Implemented builder methods for each field:
  - `processing_mode(ProcessingMode) -> Self`
  - `resolution_strategy(ConflictResolutionStrategy) -> Self`
  - `validate_effects(bool) -> Self`  
  - `max_retriggered_effects(u32) -> Self`
- ✅ Added `build() -> ProcessingContext` method
- ✅ Added `ProcessingContext::builder() -> ProcessingContextBuilder` constructor
- ✅ Added comprehensive tests for builder functionality (13 new tests)
- ✅ Added detailed documentation with usage examples
- ✅ Maintained full backward compatibility with existing API

## API Example
```rust
let context = ProcessingContext::builder()
    .processing_mode(ProcessingMode::Delayed)
    .resolution_strategy(ConflictResolutionStrategy::Maximum)
    .validate_effects(false)
    .max_retriggered_effects(50)
    .build();
```

## Benefits
- **Improved Developer Experience**: Fluent API with method chaining
- **Better Discoverability**: Configuration options are self-documenting
- **Enhanced Readability**: More intuitive configuration code
- **Future-Proof**: Easy to extend with new configuration fields
- **Backward Compatible**: Existing code continues to work unchanged

## Testing
- ✅ All existing tests pass (390 tests)
- ✅ Added 13 comprehensive builder tests covering:
  - Default value behavior
  - Fluent API chaining
  - Partial configuration
  - All enum variants
  - Clone and Debug traits
  - Backward compatibility
- ✅ Code passes all linting (clippy) and formatting (rustfmt) checks

## Acceptance Criteria Verification
All requirements from issue #212 have been met:
- ✅ ProcessingContextBuilder struct created
- ✅ Builder methods for each field implemented
- ✅ build() method added
- ✅ ProcessingContext::builder() constructor added
- ✅ Comprehensive tests added
- ✅ Documentation with usage examples added
- ✅ Backward compatibility maintained

author: alees24
body:
This PR permits the HyperBus Memory Controller (a.k.a HyperRAM) to be used in simulation with a clocking scheme and timing that much more closely models the HyperRAM activity on the FPGA board. More importantly it makes possible the development and testing in simulation of improved HyperRAM access.

 - Modify the simulator control test bench to support multiple clocks of different frequencies and phases; the HBMC requires three different clock signals, having specific phase relationships, and all of a different frequency from the Sonata system clock. This change also permits better modelling of the USB connectivity.
 - Introduce build switches `USE_SEPARATED_CLOCKS` and `USE_HYPERRAM_SIM_MODEL` which must be presented to both the C++ test bench and the SystemVerilog design; see `sonata.core`.
 - Model the Xilinx primitives used in the HBMC implementation. These models are not complete but work well enough for the vendored HBMC design to be simulated without any source modification.
 - Add a model of the HyperRAM W956D8 device used on the Sonata FPGA board.

The existing HyperRAM tests all pass with either the SRAM model (USE_HYPERRAM_SIM_MODEL) - as before - or the HBMC-controlled W956 simulation model. To test the latter the following patch may be applied, since the sonata.core file has been set up to preserve the earlier behaviour and favour faster simulations:
```
--- a/sonata.core
+++ b/sonata.core
@@ -173,7 +173,7 @@ targets:
           - '--trace-structs'
           - '--trace-params'
           - '--trace-max-array 1024'
-          - '-CFLAGS "-Wall -DVM_TRACE_FMT_FST -DTOPLEVEL_NAME=top_verilator -DUSE_HYPERRAM_SIM_MODEL"'
+          - '-CFLAGS "-Wall -DVM_TRACE_FMT_FST -DTOPLEVEL_NAME=top_verilator -DUSE_SEPARATED_CLOCKS"'
           # Add "-DUSE_SEPARATED_CLOCKS" to CFLAGS for a more accurate simulation.
           - '-LDFLAGS "-pthread -lutil -lelf"'
           - "-Wall"
@@ -182,9 +182,8 @@ targets:
           # Verilator without increasing the unroll count (see Verilator#1266)
           - "--unroll-count 72"
     parameters:
-      - USE_SEPARATED_CLOCKS=false
+      - USE_SEPARATED_CLOCKS=true
       - PRIM_DEFAULT_IMPL=prim_pkg::ImplGeneric
-      - USE_HYPERRAM_SIM_MODEL=true
 
   lint:
     <<: *default_target
```

author: edu-muller
body:
## Two commits, the first being the core functionality, while the second is an optional enhancement.

### feat: Add support for Socket.IO types

Added support for using Socket.IO typing.

This includes native methods as well as `ngx-socket-io`'s own methods.

The _README.md_ has been updated to include usage examples and a reference [link](https://socket.io/docs/v4/typescript/) to the Socket.IO docs describing usage with TypeScript.

Some types have been exported in _index.ts_ for cases where _WrappedSocket_ is extended and its methods need to be overridden.

**BREAKING**: Only this commit breaks the typing previously supported by `ngx-socket-io`.


### feat: Combine Socket.IO typing with inline typing

This enhancement combines Socket.IO typing with the inline typing previously supported by `ngx-socket-io`.

It should be compatible with both the typing from version **4.8.2** and earlier, as well as the typing from version **4.8.3** and later (when there was a breaking change).

Fixes the error `Expected 2 type arguments, but got 1.` caused by the type change since version **4.8.3**.

_README.md_ changed to include usage examples with inline typing.

## Overview
This PR introduces a comprehensive blockchain-based utility management system built on Stacks using Clarity smart contracts. The system provides decentralized solutions for managing public utility services including water, gas, and electricity.

## Features Added

### 🏗️ Core Smart Contracts

#### 1. Meter Reading Automation (`meter-reading.clar`)
- **Automated meter registration** for water, gas, and electric utilities
- **Reading submission and validation** with usage calculations
- **Authorization system** for meter readers
- **Meter lifecycle management** (activation/deactivation)
- **Usage period calculations** for billing integration

**Key Functions:**
- `register-meter`: Register new utility meters
- `submit-reading`: Submit and validate meter readings
- `authorize-reader`: Manage authorized meter readers
- `get-usage-for-period`: Calculate usage between dates

#### 2. Bill Generation (`bill-generation.clar`)
- **Customer registration and management**
- **Dynamic bill generation** with configurable rate schedules
- **Multi-utility billing** (water, gas, electric) with separate base fees
- **Due date management** with late fee calculations
- **Bill status tracking** (paid/unpaid)

**Key Functions:**
- `register-customer`: Register new customers
- `generate-bill`: Create monthly utility bills
- `update-rate-schedule`: Modify utility rates
- `mark-bill-paid`: Update payment status

#### 3. Payment Processing (`payment-processing.clar`)
- **Multi-channel payment support** (online, mail, in-person)
- **Processing fee management** by payment method
- **Customer balance tracking** with payment history
- **Refund processing** with partial/full refund support
- **Autopay setup** capabilities

**Key Functions:**
- `process-payment`: Handle customer payments
- `process-refund`: Process payment refunds
- `setup-autopay`: Configure automatic payments
- `update-payment-method`: Manage payment options

#### 4. Disconnection Management (`disconnection-management.clar`)
- **Service connection lifecycle** management
- **Disconnection notice system** with due dates
- **Grace period protection** for essential services
- **Reconnection request processing** with fee calculations
- **Service status tracking** throughout the process

**Key Functions:**
- `initialize-service`: Set up new service connections
- `issue-disconnection-notice`: Send disconnection warnings
- `execute-disconnection`: Disconnect services for non-payment
- `request-reconnection`: Process reconnection requests

#### 5. Budget Billing (`budget-billing.clar`)
- **Budget plan enrollment** with averaged monthly payments
- **Monthly payment tracking** with late fee calculations
- **Usage recording** for reconciliation purposes
- **Annual reconciliation** with refunds/additional charges
- **Plan management** (suspend, reactivate, cancel)

**Key Functions:**
- `enroll-budget-billing`: Enroll customers in budget plans
- `record-monthly-payment`: Track budget payments
- `perform-reconciliation`: Annual true-up process
- `adjust-monthly-amount`: Modify payment amounts

### 🧪 Comprehensive Test Suite

#### Test Coverage Includes:
- **Unit tests** for all contract functions
- **Integration scenarios** across contracts
- **Error handling** validation
- **Edge case testing** for boundary conditions
- **Data validation** testing

- `meter-reading.test.js`: Meter registration and reading submission
- `bill-generation.test.js`: Customer management and bill creation
- `payment-processing.test.js`: Payment handling and refunds

- `budget-billing.test.js`: Budget plan management and reconciliation

### 📋 Configuration & Documentation

- **Clarinet.toml**: Contract deployment configuration
- **package.json**: Node.js dependencies and scripts
- **README.md**: Comprehensive system documentation

- **System architecture** overview

- **Installation and setup** instructions

- **Authorization checks** for sensitive operations

### 💰 Economic Model

body:
## Summary
- Fixes issue #401: The Register gives 403 error due to User-Agent blocking
- **Improved approach**: Updates DefaultHandler to use proper browser headers for ALL requests
- Also fixes similar User-Agent blocking issues with Bleeping Computer and other sites

## Root Cause
Many sites (The Register, Bleeping Computer, etc.) block requests from the default Go HTTP client User-Agent (`Go-http-client/1.1`), returning 403 Forbidden or 429 Too Many Requests errors.

## Solution
**Updated approach - much cleaner than original:**

Instead of creating site-specific handlers, this PR fixes the root cause by updating `DefaultHandler` to:
- Use proper browser headers from the same config used by other handlers
- Add 10-second timeout (consistent with existing handlers)
- Improve error handling with `log.Errorf` instead of `log.Fatalf`

## Benefits
✅ **Broader fix**: Solves User-Agent blocking for ALL sites, not just The Register  
✅ **Cleaner code**: No code duplication or site-specific workarounds  
✅ **Consistent**: Follows the same header pattern as existing handlers  
✅ **Future-proof**: Automatically handles other sites with similar blocking  

## Evidence of Fix
- **The Register URL test**: Successfully extracts "Messages, Dialer apps sent text, call info to Google"
- **Previously failing tests now pass**: Bleeping Computer and Yahoo Finance tests that expected 403/429 errors now work
- **No regressions**: All other existing functionality continues to work

## Summary
This PR adds support for AWS Bedrock integration and includes missing dependencies for enhanced LLM functionality in Biomni.

## Changes Made

### 1. Enhanced Database Query Support (`biomni/tool/database.py`)
- **Added AWS Bedrock Support**: Integrated `AnthropicBedrock` client for AWS Bedrock compatibility
- **Environment Variable Support**: Added support for AWS credentials (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN`)
- **Flexible Client Initialization**: The `_query_claude_for_api` function now supports both direct Anthropic API and AWS Bedrock
- **Model Name Mapping**: Automatic mapping of model names for AWS Bedrock (e.g., `claude-3-5-haiku-20241022` → `anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0`)

### 2. Environment Dependencies (`biomni_env/environment.yml`)
- ** this error happens when I try to run locally seems like missing dependencies 
- **Added `langchain_aws`**: Included the missing AWS integration package for LangChain 
- **Enhanced LLM Support**: This enables seamless integration with AWS Bedrock services

### 3. Software Installation Script (`biomni_env/new_software_v004.sh`)
- **Updated Installation**: Added `langchain_aws` to the pip installation command
- **Consistent Dependencies**: Ensures all required packages are installed in the environment

## Technical Details

### AWS Bedrock Integration
The changes allow Biomni to use AWS Bedrock as an alternative to direct Anthropic API calls. This is particularly useful for:
- Organizations with existing AWS infrastructure
- Cost optimization through AWS pricing
- Enhanced security through AWS IAM controls
- Compliance requirements that mandate AWS services

### Backward Compatibility
- All existing functionality remains unchanged
- Direct Anthropic API calls continue to work as before

author: copilot
body:
The model catalog was missing several latest AI models that were released in 2025, causing them to be unavailable in the Settings dropdown selections. Users reported that key models like `grok-3-fast`, `grok-4-0709`, and other recent releases were not appearing in the Chat Model Name dropdown when selecting providers.

## Problem
The screenshot shows the xAI provider selected but missing several Grok models that should be available:

![Settings dropdown missing models](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffbdb0e1-af90-47f8-b359-bf828cc8ec6b)

## Solution
Updated `framework/helpers/model_catalog.py` to add 16 missing latest models across three major providers:

### xAI Models Added (3)
- `grok-3-fast` → "Grok 3 Fast"  
- `grok-3-mini-fast` → "Grok 3 Mini Fast"
- `grok-4-0709` → "Grok 4 (0709)"

### OpenAI Models Added (9)
- `gpt-4.1-mini` → "GPT-4.1 Mini"
- `gpt-4.1-nano` → "GPT-4.1 Nano" 
- `o3-mini-2025-01-31` → "o3 Mini (2025-01-31)"
- `o3-pro` → "o3 Pro"
- `gpt-4o-audio` → "GPT-4o Audio"
- `gpt-4o-mini-audio` → "GPT-4o Mini Audio"
- `computer-use-preview` → "Computer Use Preview"
- `gpt-4o-search-preview` → "GPT-4o Search Preview"
- `gpt-4o-mini-search-preview` → "GPT-4o Mini Search Preview"

### Google Models Added (4)
- `gemini-2.0-flash` → "Gemini 2.0 Flash"
- `gemini-2.0-flash-thinking-exp` → "Gemini 2.0 Flash Thinking Exp"
- `gemini-2.0-pro-experimental` → "Gemini 2.0 Pro Experimental"
- `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` → "Gemini 2.0 Flash Lite"

## Impact
- **xAI Provider**: 6 → 9 models (+50% increase)
- **OpenAI Provider**: 23 → 32 models (+39% increase)  
- **Google Provider**: 7 → 11 models (+57% increase)
- **Zero breaking changes**: All existing models continue to work
- **Immediate availability**: Models appear in UI dropdowns via existing API

Users can now select the latest 2025 AI models that were previously missing from the dropdown selections.

Fixes #134.

author: maxghenis
body:
## Description

Fixes #51 (again)

The previous fix was merged but users reported the clipboard functionality still wasn't working. This PR adds a more robust fallback mechanism.

## Problem

When embedded in an iframe on PolicyEngine, the modern Clipboard API can fail due to:
- Browser security restrictions
- Permission denials
- Cross-origin iframe limitations

## Solution

This PR implements a multi-tier approach:

1. **Primary**: Try the modern Clipboard API
2. **Fallback**: If that fails, create a temporary textarea element and use the older `document.execCommand('copy')` method
3. **Last resort**: If both fail, show an alert with the URL so users can manually copy it

## Changes

- Replaced the simple query string fallback with a textarea-based copy method
- Added proper error handling for each tier
- Maintains visual feedback ("Copied\!" button state) for successful copies
- Logs detailed debug information to help diagnose issues

## Testing

1. Visit https://policyengine.org/us/obbba-household-explorer  
2. Open browser console (F12)
3. Navigate to any household
4. Click the 🔗 button
5. Check console for one of these outcomes:
   - "Successfully copied URL to clipboard" (primary method worked)
   - "Clipboard API failed" followed by "Successfully copied using execCommand fallback" (fallback worked)
   - Alert dialog with the URL (both methods failed)

The clipboard should now contain the full URL in all supported browsers and iframe contexts.

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a complete iOS Password Manager application that meets all the requirements specified in the issue:

## 🔐 Master Key Authentication
- **Primary login method**: App requires only master key for authentication
- **Secure validation**: Minimum 8-character requirement with proper validation
- **First-time setup**: Automatic secure storage of master key on initial use

## 📱 QR Code Integration
- **Desktop app integration**: Scan QR codes from desktop password manager for seamless authentication
- **Camera integration**: Built-in QR scanner with proper permission handling (`NSCameraUsageDescription`)
- **Visual feedback**: Clear scanning interface with guidance and cancel options

## 👤 Face ID/Touch ID Support
- **Biometric authentication**: Full Face ID and Touch ID support using `LocalAuthentication` framework
- **User choice prompt**: App asks users if they want to enable biometric authentication
- **Secure fallback**: Falls back to master key if biometric authentication fails
- **Permission handling**: Proper Face ID usage description (`NSFaceIDUsageDescription`)

## 🏦 Heavy Encryption Storage
- **Military-grade encryption**: AES-GCM encryption using Apple's `CryptoKit` framework
- **Key derivation**: SHA256 hash-based key derivation from master key
- **iOS Keychain**: Secure storage using iOS Keychain services with device-specific protection
- **Biometric protection**: Optional biometric-protected keychain entries

## 📋 Copy to Clipboard Features
- **Universal clipboard**: Copy buttons for all password fields (title, username, password, website)
- **One-tap copying**: Quick access using `UIPasteboard` without revealing sensitive data
- **Secure display**: Passwords shown as dots with copy functionality

## 🛡️ Security Architecture
```swift
// Example of the encryption implementation
private func encryptData(_ data: Data, with key: String) -> Data? {
    let hashedKey = SHA256.hash(data: key.data(using: .utf8)!)
    let symmetricKey = SymmetricKey(data: hashedKey)
    return try? AES.GCM.seal(data, using: symmetricKey).combined
}
```

## 📱 iOS Features
- **SwiftUI interface**: Modern, native iOS user experience
- **Complete Xcode project**: Ready-to-build iOS application with proper project structure
- **Asset management**: App icons and color sets configured
- **iOS 15+ support**: Compatible with modern iOS versions
- **iPad support**: Universal app supporting both iPhone and iPad

## 🧪 Testing & Validation
- **Core logic tests**: Validated password generation, encryption, and data handling
- **Swift syntax validation**: All code verified for correctness
- **Comprehensive documentation**: Detailed README with setup and usage instructions

## Project Structure
```
iOSPasswordManager/
├── App.swift                 # Main app entry point
├── Views/
│   ├── ContentView.swift     # Password list and main interface
│   ├── LoginView.swift       # Authentication interface
│   └── QRScannerView.swift   # QR code scanning functionality
├── Models/
│   └── PasswordManager.swift # Core password management logic
├── Services/
│   ├── KeychainService.swift # Secure storage operations
│   └── BiometricAuth.swift   # Biometric authentication handling
└── Assets.xcassets/          # App icons and visual assets
```

The implementation uses only native iOS frameworks and follows Apple's security best practices for password management applications.

Fixes #5.

### **User description** ## Overview This PR refactors the plugin system to have a clearer architecture with explicit stages and improved location tracking. The main focus was on making the MathPlugin simpler and more reliable, achieving 100% location finding success rate. ## Major Changes ### 1. Clear 5-Stage Pipeline - **Stage 1: EXTRACT** - Find items of interest in text chunks - **Stage 2: INVESTIGATE** - Validate and add severity/messages - **Stage 3: LOCATE** - Find exact positions in document - **Stage 4: ANALYZE** - Generate insights and patterns - **Stage 5: GENERATE** - Create UI comments ### 2. Improved Architecture - Renamed `ChunkFinding` to `LocatedFinding` for clarity - Created numbered stage directories (`01_extract`, `02_investigate`, etc.) - Moved finding storage from BasePlugin to individual plugins with type safety - Extracted all functionality into testable utility functions ### 3. Closes #1 

This PR introduces the foundational data models for the application by defining the initial Prisma schema. This structure will support all core features planned for the MVP.

### Schema Changes
- Creates the `User` model to store user credentials and information.
- Creates the `Book` model to store book data retrieved from external APIs.
- Introduces `BookshelfItem` as a "join model" to manage the many-to-many relationship between users and books on their shelves.
- Adds the `Review` model to handle user-submitted reviews for books.

This provides the necessary database structure for the upcoming authentication and bookshelf features.

author: zliel
body:
# Brief Overview

<!-- Describe the purpose of this pull request -->

In this pull request, I added support for raw HTML in input Markdown files, and fixed bugs involving line grouping.

## More Details

<!-- Describe the changes made in this pull request -->

- There is a new `Token::RawHtmlTag` variant
- There is a new `MdBlockElement::RawHtml` variant
- Lines that begin with spaces now properly group with previous lines (i.e. text, space-indented elements, etc.)
- Lines that begin with tabs and start with HTML will now group with previous lines if they also started with HTML
- The README has been updated with information about using raw HTML as input
  - More specifically, it warns that currently Mark-rs does not sanitize the HTML so that users can use tags like `<script>`, `<embed>`, etc.
  - However, these tags make pages potentially vulnerable to XSS attacks, so there is a warning regarding raw HTML and links to [OWASP](https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/xss/) and the [OWASP XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet.](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) for more information

## Test Updates

<!-- Describe the tests that you created for this pull request -->

- There are new tests for tokenizing, parsing, and generating HTML for raw HTML input
- There are tests for using both Markdown and raw HTML in a line
